title.en: Using AI: Can We Trust AI?

narrative_brief: Mini PechaKucha for Science Communication (SDG 9 × AI Literacy × Science Communication)

title.zh: 引言，連結 SDG 9 與 AI

A2.text: Good morning. Today I talk about SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure. It asks every country in the world to make things well and to try new ideas.
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate
A2.basis: Full rewrite. The previous overlay kept most of the workbook A2 column, which sat above the A2 band on Flesch-Kincaid and long-word load on seven slides and ran over the 20-second clock on three. This version is written from the source meaning, slide by slide, in present-simple spoken English with one idea per sentence, and it shares almost no content words with the B1 and B2 texts, so the three levels are three texts rather than one text in three coats. Meaning, slide order and every named fact are unchanged: SDG 9 Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure; ChatGPT; Gemini; AI hallucination; Google Scholar; PubMed. Technical corrections: the workbook A2 says AI 'only guesses the next word' and that 'sometimes the formulas and data are completely wrong'. A language model predicts the most likely next word from patterns in the text it was trained on, and what it fabricates is sources, not arithmetic, so those lines are restated as prediction and as invented sources. Nothing here says the model knows, understands or looks anything up.

B1.workbook_text: Good morning, everyone. Today, I would like to explore SDG 9, which focuses on industry, innovation, and infrastructure. Globally, building strong infrastructures is essential for driving scientific progress and economic growth.

B2.text: Good morning. The ninth Sustainable Development Goal, Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, asks every country in the world to build the factories, the networks and the kind of research that a modern economy quietly depends on.
B2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate
B2.basis: Replaces the workbook B2 column, which reached for C1 vocabulary ('revolutionary infrastructure', 'exceptionally efficient', 'deceptive data') while its syntax stayed at B1: no concession, no passive and no participle clauses. Meaning, slide order and every named fact are unchanged: SDG 9 Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure; ChatGPT and Gemini (slide 3 keeps them as the tools students use); AI hallucination; Google Scholar; PubMed; peer-reviewed journals. Technical corrections: the workbook says the model 'confidently fabricates deceptive data', which attributes intent and confidence to a program, and that it predicts words 'based on patterns learned from enormous amounts of text', which is right but sits beside the claim that it 'does not truly understand science' as if that were an accident. B2.workbook_text: Good morning, everyone. Today, let’s examine United Nations SDG 9, a global framework dedicated to upgrading industry, driving innovation, and building resilient infrastructure. This initiative challenges us to utilize cutting-edge technologies to foster sustainable development across all scientific fields worldwide.

A prime example is "AI hallucination," a phenomenon where the algorithm confidently fabricates deceptive data, nonexistent citations, and false scientific assertions that appear entirely authentic.

B2.workbook_text: Why does this happen? Large language models do not truly understand science. Instead, they generate responses by predicting the most probable sequence of words based on patterns learned from enormous amounts of text.
